title: Declarative Patchlet Forge for Support Playbooks
creator: Amelia Johnson
description:
Build a 'Patchlet Forge' — a declarative authoring and execution layer that converts small, verifiable remediation snippets (patchlets) into task graph steps inside support playbooks. Goal: let SREs and Support write concise YAML/JSON patchlets that declare intent (check, mutate, rollback) and get compiled into idempotent, observable tasks that run in the existing runbook executor. This reduces on-call cognitive overhead and accelerates safe fixes without shipping large runbooks.

Scope: authoring spec + compiler + runtime adapters + telemetry + CI checks. Not in scope: full UI editor (thin UX hooks only), RBAC model changes, or cross-cluster orchestration in this phase.
acceptance_criteria: Patchlet spec v1 defined and documented in Confluence with examples for common remediation classes (env var fix, rollout pause, small db migration)
Compiler translates patchlet into task graph JSON accepted by runbook executor with idempotency checksum
Automated preflight validation (static type checks + dry-run fn) integrated into CI pipeline
Runtime adapter emits structured telemetry (patchlet_id, step_hash, success, duration) to ops-telemetry and can be visualized in Console
Three internal playbooks converted to patchlets and exercised in staging without service regressions
implementation_notes: Spec design: minimal declarative primitives (check, apply, compensate, gate) to keep surface area small
Compiler: Rust prototype (existing runbook infra library) + JS microshim for embedding in the console build
Runtime: use existing step executor; add patchlet idempotency layer that stores per-patchlet markers in Redis with TTL
CI: add 'patchlet-lint' job to GitHub Actions that runs static validation + 'dry-run' using a local fake-executor
Telemetry: extend 'ops.telemetry' schema with fields: patchlet_name, version, author, result_code, duration_ms
test_plan: Unit: compile 50 synthetic patchlets derived from historical incidents; ensure deterministic taskgraph output
Integration: run compiled patchlets against staging clusters; assert no side effects beyond intended mutations
Chaos: inject network loss during patchlet apply steps to validate compensate paths and retries
E2E: convert 3 frequent support workflows to patchlets and run in canary; collect metrics for error rate and mean time to repair
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): expose feature to internal SREs + 3 support engineers using CLI + repo-based patchlet catalog
Phase 2 (wider): onboard Operations team, add console integration for viewing patchlet manifests and last-run telemetry
Phase 3 (GA): enable team-level RBAC gating, expand catalog, add onboarding docs and workspace templates
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: faulty patchlet causes unintended mutation — Mitigation: default to dry-run fail-open, require at least one manual approval gate for high-impact patchlets
Risk: patchlet authoring confusion — Mitigation: provide templates and a patchlet-lint ruleset with clear errors and examples
Risk: telemetry volume spike — Mitigation: sample low-severity runs and enforce telemetry cardinality limits
metrics: Adoption: number of patchlets authored per week
Safety: percent of patchlet runs requiring human rollback
Efficiency: median time from incident detection to fix when using patchlet vs current runbook
Cost: average execution token/time saved by converting frequent runbooks to patchlets
